properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, in his own words: "one idea that I've come across is that I work many inter-related projects. it seems like a reflow2 project/graph is limited to one git repo. curious if we should remove this constraint? then I can use the reflow2 graph in one project (project_x) and still use it to guide a closely related project (say project_y). the benefit of this is that a set of projects done in this manner can all influence each other. another option is to build the reflow2 graph in the parent folder of a bunch of interrelated projects. for instance, all my individual projects are in a folder called git_projects - maybe this is the appropriate place to build the graph versus within each project."

⭐ FIRST, THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, AND THAT MATTERS BEFORE ANY OPTION IS WEIGHED. There is NO CONSTRAINT TO REMOVE. `--graph-path` is an ordinary CLI argument; this repo's `.mcp.json` passes `./.reflow2/graph` and that is a CONVENTION, not a binding. Verified the same day by creating graphs at arbitrary filesystem paths outside any repository during the corpus trial. `dec:install-once-per-machine` already states the position: "reflow2 installs once per machine; the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share." So the question is not CAN the graph live elsewhere — it can, today, with no change — but WHERE IT SHOULD, which is a design question about authority rather than a limitation to lift.

SECOND, THE PLACEMENT RULE IS ALREADY DECIDED AND IT DISPOSES OF ONE OPTION OUTRIGHT. `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED, Anthony, 2026-07-25): "A design is its own graph when something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED — and a subtree of one graph otherwise. THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT DECIDE; AUTHORITY DOES." A `git_projects/` parent folder is a filesystem convention with no authority attached, so under the accepted rule it is NOT a reason to put a graph there. If those projects share a graph it must be because they share an owner, a release train or a recipient — never because they share a directory.

⭐ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHY THE QUESTION IS GENUINELY OPEN RATHER THAN ALREADY ANSWERED: THE RULE WAS WRITTEN FOR FEDERATION BETWEEN OWNERS, AND ANTHONY'S CASE IS ONE OWNER WITH MANY RELEASE TRAINS. The discriminator is a three-way OR — owned, released, OR shared — so "separately released" alone sends his projects to separate graphs. But every cost the rule cites for a seam (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) is a cost of crossing an AUTHORITY boundary, and there is no authority boundary here. He is paying federation's price to solve a filing problem. The rule is not wrong; his case sits on a seam in it that multi-org federation never presented.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ONE GRAPH FOR THE FAMILY, levels inside it. The accepted rule already blesses this "for everything inside one ownership boundary" and `cap:scoped-analysis` delivers per-level reading, so nothing new is needed. Counter, from the rule's own text: what one graph cannot give is separate write locks, separate release trains, or a way to share ONE project without shipping the others — and his projects DO release separately, which is exactly the case (a) was said not to cover. (b) A GRAPH PER PROJECT, MIRRORED. What the accepted rule prescribes, and the linking half is BUILT (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:publish-surface`). Counter: `dec:linked-repos-poc` names the blocker — "reflow2 structures roughly one and a half of the six characteristics an interface spec needs and puts the rest in one free-text string, so today two graphs can be linked and still not be comparable" — and reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 of 73, so the mechanism this option rests on is the least-exercised thing in the design. (c) A GRAPH IN THE PARENT FOLDER. Ruled out by `dec:nested-graphs` as stated, but worth keeping visible because it is what Anthony reached for and the reason it fails is not obvious: a folder is where things SIT, not who decides them. (d) ONE GRAPH FOR INTENT, SEPARATE GRAPHS FOR BUILD. Not previously considered: the shared thing across his projects is what he is trying to achieve, and the separate thing is what each repo ships. Counter: reflow2 has no vocabulary for a design that holds only intent and no build, and `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` is the closest thing — which is about a corpus, not a standing hub. (e) DO NOTHING; the constraint he wanted removed does not exist, and he can point `--graph-path` wherever he likes today. Counter: that answers the mechanism and ignores the question, which is what SHOULD be one design.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:nested-graphs` and its four stated obligations (the coordinate, the roll-up, freshness, the seam), `dec:linked-repos-poc` and its dependency on `req:interface-spec-complete`, `req:design-composes` and `req:composed-analysis` (both accepted), and `cap:mirror-surface`/`cap:publish-surface`/`cap:composed-analysis` (all built). The LINKING half exists; the COMPARING half does not.

NOT CHECKED, and it bears directly on (b): whether `mirror_surface` and `compose_and_analyse` have ever been run on two real designs. `dec:linked-repos-poc` is one of the two parked Decisions that `detect_defects` has been reporting as governing nothing all session, which suggests not.
properties.name: OPEN — where does the graph live when ONE PERSON works many interrelated projects, which is the case dec:nested-graphs' rule was not written for?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the search he asked for was run first — he said "I know we've discussed linking projects in the past, so there should already be some discussion on this," and he was right. Recording what already exists BEFORE recording the new question is the whole point of the exercise, and this project has spent a session establishing that the expensive failure is re-deriving what is written down.

The premise correction is on the node rather than left in conversation because it is the most perishable part: "the graph is limited to one git repo" is a reasonable thing to believe from the outside, it is false, and nothing in the repo says so plainly. If that correction lives only in a chat it will be believed again.

Deliberately NOT registered as formal alternatives — that would make this a fork the loop starts asking him to choose between, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs because that one asks what may cross a boundary and this one asks where the boundary is; one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.
